summary: ```markdown # The Designer's CLO Journey: The Production of Pleats ## Introduction Hello, everyone. Good evening! Can you hear my voice? Our live broadcast tonight is about to start. My name is Stella, and I'm from Shanghai. Today, I will give you a self-introduction and share some knowledge about folding. ## Overview of Folding Today's content revolves around the basic knowledge of folding. We will explore a specific style and its extension transformation, as well as the styles of the fan and the flower-shaped fold. Let’s begin the live broadcast. ## Understanding the Style You can see our style here. This design primarily focuses on the fan and flower-shaped folds. First, let me explain the basic principles of folding to give everyone a general impression. We are currently in a simulation state. ### Modifying the Internal Line Angle Now, I will modify the first inner line of a vertical angle. Watch closely as I make the vertical angle smaller; you’ll see the tabletop in the three-way window becoming more pronounced. Adjusting the internal line angle makes the plate emerge more and more inward. When we modify the internal line angle, we can not only adjust colors but also shorten the design. Let’s take a look at how to fold the foldable part by adjusting the foldable angle of the internal line. The foldable part consists of three internal lines: 0 degrees, 360 degrees, and 180 degrees, respectively. ### Effects of Different Angles The 0-degree line protrudes outwards, creating a red effect, while the 360-degree line pushes inward. As long as it is large, the internal line less than 180 degrees will appear green. The 180-degree line can be hooked or not. Next, let's adjust the angle of the foldable part. Set the first line to 0 degrees and the second line to 360 degrees. When we open the foldable line, we can observe an auto-folding effect in the 3D window, making the angle of the foldable part smoother. ## Sewing the Foldable Part Now, let's discuss how to sew the foldable part. When sewing, we select the first line to be sewn, which is the line before the zero degree. I will use the freedom sewing tool to sew it while holding down the Shift key. Additionally, we will sew the third line before the zero degree. You can see that our guide is already sewn. Switching to the back side, we can see that this fold is not sewn. We need to sew the pocket. Let’s see how we sew the fold again. The edges at the zero degree must be aligned, with the lines on both sides of the zero degrees directed similarly. The lines on both sides of 360 degrees must also be in the same direction, but the paper's direction must be opposite. ### Finalizing the Sewing Process Now, let’s sew the folds. We need to modify the direction of the paper to create the fold. In the 3D window, the fold is already sewn. Now, let’s sew the second line on both sides of the paper while ensuring the paper's direction is correct. The fold has transitioned from one side to another smoothly. Let’s mask the measure selection. As we can see, we have finished sewing the first fold, and the other folds now slide into place naturally. ## Folding Techniques Now, I will demonstrate how to crop the edges. The internal lines consist of 360 degrees, 0 degrees, 180 degrees, and repeat. These internal lines form a complete ruler. When explaining the ruler, we don’t need to modify each line individually. ### Using the Ruler Tool Here, I will show you how to fold and use the ruler. Press the left button on the left side of the ruler to turn it over, then double-click to finish. While clicking, ensure we cross these internal lines that we want to turn over. The default line is vertical. When we select the vertical line, the angle of the fold changes slightly, similar to what we see in our presentation slides. Each ruler has several internal lines, and you can choose 2 or 3. The difference lies in whether the internal line of 180 degrees is included. ### Adjusting the Ruler If it includes the internal line of 180 degrees, we need to select 3; if not, we select 2. This rule applies to both vertical and horizontal rulers. Let’s switch back to the horizontal ruler and click OK. Our internal line has been folded. Now, we can use the sewing ruler tool to sew. When sewing the ruler, it automatically detects 3 lines as a complete ruler. So, when sewing this board, it automatically detects the last line as a complete ruler. ## Creating Skirt Panels Next, we will create the bottom skirt panel. After we have arranged the panel, we will sew the bottom skirt panel with the top skirt panel. We can adjust the shoulder strap of the panel and modify the clothing slightly. We will check for any holes in the fabric before stopping the simulation. ### Adding Foldable Panels Now, we need to use the foldable tool to add the foldable panel to the bottom skirt panel. Left-click on the panel outline, then click again to select the side that needs to be folded. Enter the width of the foldable panel and its number. I created a foldable panel equal in width at both ends, comprising 20 folds. After rearranging the panel, we can see that it automatically sews our sewing line since we've already sewn the panel beforehand. ### Finalizing the Panel Arrangement Let’s look at the arrangement points on the model and ensure it is positioned correctly. When there is a foldable panel, we need to harden it before modeling to avoid conflicts. Now, we will simulate the design. After improving the quality of the clothing, we can check the effect and adjust the clothing state. ## Changing Fabrics Now let’s change the fabric to a piece of real silk. During the molding process, it will become more viscous and thinner. We can also modify the transparency of this fabric in the water-cooling machine. ### Rendering and Textures Let’s open the high-quality rendering to see its effect. Then we can copy a piece of fabric and apply it to the shoulder plate. Replace its texture with a real silk texture, and adjust the color to a lighter pink. Next, we will adjust the strength of the hairline and modify its material type to metal. This will give it a glowing effect by adjusting its metal density and reflection intensity. ## Final Adjustments With the style nearly finished, we’ll change the shoes to match the clothes and modify the posture to see the overall effect. After improving the quality of the clothing, we can take a look at its effect and adjust the state of the clothing dress. ### Creating the Fan Next, we will explain how to create a fan. We will download the style of our main picture. I previously used the 3D pen model tool to create this top coat. Now, we will begin by making the bottom coat using the 3D pen tool. #### Designing the Top Coat According to the width of the top coat and the length of the skirt, we will create the dimensions for the top coat. The width is 195x1200, and we will create the front coat. Then we will create the back coat using the same method. ## Final Remarks Thank you for tuning in to our session on the production of pleats using CLO. I hope you found this insightful and that it will help you in your design journey. If you have any questions, feel free to ask. Thanks for watching! ```
